new_claims.subject: work:milligan_2022
new_claims.statement: Milligan distinguishes the field of Digital History from wider digitized historical practice and identifies public-history and quantitative traditions among its lineages.
new_claims.qualification: Selected section 1.3, pp. 7–8; an attributed retrospective account of plural roots, not a single founding date or an influence arrow from every earlier tradition.

review.rationale: Bounded source-based proposal pending release acceptance.

evidence.support: Milligan separates a specialist field from broad digitized practices and discusses multiple earlier traditions.
evidence.limitation: The cited earlier works are not independently read in this batch; this is Milligan’s 2022 assessment.

new_claims.subject: work:cohen_rosenzweig_digital_2005
new_claims.statement: Cohen and Rosenzweig connect digital history with searchable and recombinable evidence, public participation and collaborative historical communication, while examining problems of authenticity and authority.
new_claims.qualification: Selected introduction only. Their account identifies possibilities and hazards, not proof that digital access automatically democratizes history; historical platform examples are not current measurements.

new_claims.subject: work:thomas_computing_2004

new_claims.qualification: Selected concluding discussion, not endorsement of every earlier genealogy in the chapter. He describes an experimental programme and project design, not an inevitable transformation of the profession.

new_claims.subject: work:thomas_ayers_differences_2003
new_claims.statement: Thomas and Ayers frame a close comparison of two American communities around the relationship between slavery and emergent modernity, asking why profound social differences can coexist with similar measurable indices.
new_claims.qualification: Repository author abstract only. Their stated focus is slavery’s relation to white society, not a comprehensive account of enslaved people’s lives; no replication of the comparison or full electronic-article reading is claimed.

new_claims.subject: work:blevins_future_2016
new_claims.statement: Blevins recognizes digital history’s archival, pedagogical and public achievements while calling for more explicit argument-driven academic scholarship and less rhetoric of future potential.
new_claims.qualification: An attributed 2016 disciplinary assessment, not a field-wide quantitative audit. His later discussion explicitly recognizes interpretation in public-history projects; the distinction concerns organizing priorities, not an absence of arguments.
